news.title: More than half of Americans in their 40s are sandwiched between an aging parent and their own children
news.summary_en: Overall, 25% of U.S. adults have a parent age 65 or older and have a child under 18, an adult child receiving financial support or both.

news.title: No Easy Fix for Bogus Respondents in Online Opt-In Polls
news.summary_en: A new study examining online opt-in polling finds that while removing bogus respondents generally improves data quality, no single method reliably solves the problem.

news.title: Many across 37 countries view the UN favorably, but opinions have become more negative in some places
news.summary_en: A median of 55% across 37 countries hold a favorable view of the UN, though views in some countries have turned more negative in recent years.

news.title: Fewer Americans use cash today than a decade ago, but many still carry it
news.summary_en: Today, 42% of U.S. adults say they don’t use cash for any purchases in a typical week. This is up from 24% in 2015.

news.title: Americans want transparency when AI is used in their healthcare
news.summary_en: About seven-in-ten U.S. adults (72%) say it’s extremely or very important that a doctor or other healthcare provider tells them if they’re using AI in their healthcare.

news.title: From Diagnoses to Treatments, Why Americans Use AI Chatbots for Health
news.summary_en: Americans use chatbots for a host of health-related reasons, from helping make diagnoses on their own to learning more about information they may have gotten from a doctor. Nearly all chatbot health users find this AI information helpful.

news.title: How South Koreans view their relationship with the U.S.
news.summary_en: For the first time in over 20 years, a majority of South Koreans have an unfavorable opinion of the U.S.
